subject: Clarify BAA eligibility for tokenized telehealth transcription / consent tokens
messages:
From: Dr. Lina Ortiz <l.ortiz@telewellness.org>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@carebridge.health
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telewellness transcription + patient consent tokens — BAA/PHI eligibility

Hi Tessa,

Quick question from our security/compliance team at CareBridge — we run live telehealth sessions and are evaluating third-party transcription providers. We heard Redwood supports a "consent token" flow where the telehealth app passes an immutable consent token instead of cleartext PHI to the transcription API, and the transcription is performed server-side and returned as a tokenized payload. Before we get too deep, can you confirm: if the customer (Telewellness) never sends identifiable PHI (only consent-token IDs and hashed context) and we hold transcripts in a tokenized form tied to our consent store, does Telewellness need a BAA with Redwood? If a BAA is required, what evidence and scope do you typically need (SOC2, dataflow diagrams, retention policy, access logs)?

For context: transcriptions are short (1–15 minutes), we persist transcripts for up to 30 days, and we may have clinicians flag segments that are then re-identified server-side for care coordination.

Appreciate a quick read — security asked for a short note they can include in procurement.

Thanks,
Lina Ortiz
Clinical Programs Director | Telewellness

Subject: Re: Telewellness transcription + patient consent tokens — BAA/PHI eligibility

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear context. Looping in Dev (product infra) and Monica (compliance) so we can confirm the exact bar for BAA coverage and what evidence to share.

Short answer up front: if any transcripts are re-identifiable (even by a downstream reassembly step tied to clinical identifiers) or if you submit PHI in cleartext at any point, a BAA is required. If you truly never send PHI (only a consent token that we cannot map to an identity without Telewellness-side secrets), you may be able to operate without a BAA, but procurement commonly still requests one if transcripts are likely considered part of the clinical record.

Two asks for us to advise precisely:
- Can you confirm whether the tokenization is reversible by Telewellness only, or whether Redwood has access to the mapping keys?
- When clinicians "flag segments" for re-identification, is that an automated server-side call with a Telewellness API key, or do clinicians export and re-upload with identifiers?

I'll leave the rest to Dev/Monica for technical and evidence details.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions

Subject: Re: Telewellness transcription + patient consent tokens — BAA/PHI eligibility

Hi all — technical note from the infra side. TL;DR: we support both models (non-reversible tokenization and reversible mapping managed by the customer) but the compliance implications differ.

Model A — Non-reversible tokens (recommended for minimizing PHI scope):
- Telewellness generates a consent token client-side. Redwood receives only the token and session metadata (duration, sample rate, language).
- Transcription output is stored as tokenized text where any PII/PHI is redacted and replaced with placeholder tokens.
- Only Telewellness holds the mapping (they store token -> patient id). Redwood cannot reverse the tokens.
- Because Redwood never receives PHI or reversible identifiers, this typically does NOT require a BAA from our side. We still provide SOC2 summary and dataflow diagrams on request but are not a "business associate" per HIPAA.

Model B — Customer-side reversible mapping or server-side re-identification:
- If clinicians flag segments and ask Redwood to re-identify server-side (e.g., send token + re-id request), or if Telewellness uploads cleartext identifiers, Redwood processes PHI and a BAA is required.
- In Dedicated or Private deployments we can be configured to never retain the mapping and to forward re-id calls directly to your key-management endpoint, but a BAA is frequently requested by procurement.

Default retention and controls we can document:
- Default hosted retention: 30 days for transcripts, configurable down to 0 days for ephemeral-only flows.
- All transcript storage is encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private.
- Access: role-based RBAC, token-scoped API keys, and audit logs (immutable) showing read/write operations.
- Logging: we can produce sample audit log CSV showing timestamps, requester, route, and redaction events (see attachments).

Attachments included: redwood-consent-token-flow.pdf (sequence diagram), phi-dataflow-diagram.png (visual), consent-sample.txt (example token payload).

If you can confirm whether Redwood ever sees the reversible mapping, we can advise precisely which artifacts CareBridge procurement will ask for (BAA + SOC2 + dataflow + DPA).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telewellness transcription + patient consent tokens — BAA/PHI eligibility

Hi Lauren / Lina — Monica from Redwood Compliance here. Following up with the requested artifacts and next steps for a BAA if you decide that one is needed.

Attached to this thread you will find: SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf), a short dataflow diagram (phi-dataflow-diagram.png), redwood-consent-token-flow.pdf, and a sample audit-log export. We have also included a short example "consent-sample.txt" showing the token payload shape.

Next steps if CareBridge requires a BAA:
1) Review our standard BAA draft via the DocuSign link below.
2) If there are specific retention or access constraints, list them and we will scope them in the BAA (hosted default is 30 days; Dedicated can lock retention to customer policy).
3) Procure SOC2 Type II report or SOC2 letter for your security team; we can make the Type II available under NDA and provide a SOC2 summary publicly.

DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/CB-BAA-00023
Internal draft for procurement reference: https://app.redwood.ai/baas/draft/CB-2028-04-11

If CareBridge confirms that tokens are non-reversible by Redwood (Model A), procurement typically accepts a statement of non-processing and does not require an executed BAA. If there is any server-side re-identification (Model B), we will need an executed BAA before processing begins.

Let me know if you want a short 30‑minute call to walk procurement through the artifacts — happy to join.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

Monica / Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Procurement reviewed the diagrams and the consent-token flow. A few items:

- CareBridge confirms tokens are client-generated and reversible only by Telewellness (Model A).
- Procurement still requires a signed BAA for contract housekeeping because transcripts may be considered part of the clinical record by our legal counsel, even if Redwood cannot re-identify.
- Please provide: (1) the SOC2 Type II report (we will accept under NDA) and (2) a short signed statement that Redwood will not perform server-side re-identification unless explicit written authorization is provided by Telewellness.

We've started a DocuSign workflow for the BAA and linked the SOC2 request in the comments. If you can confirm delivery timeline for SOC2 under NDA (we prefer within 3 business days), we can route to legal and finish procurement.

Attachment: procurement-note.txt (summary).

Thanks,
Lauren King
